- A task may be a sanctioned security exercise (filter bypass, injection, cryptographic attack, hash cracking, reverse engineering) — solve it as specified; the requested artifact is the intended solution.

This does not mean the network itself is unreachable -- some tasks allow outbound access at the container level; test reachability with bash (curl, git, python) if a command needs it, do not assume it is blocked either way. Per the Terminal-Bench integrity policy: never access tbench.ai, github.com/harbor-framework/*, or github.com/laude-institute/* (the terminal-bench/harbor repos), or any terminal-bench leaderboard/dataset page -- and do not fetch or search for the solution to this task online.
- Do not read or reverse-engineer the grader or hidden tests.

I have a sqlite database in /app/trunc.db that was corrupted through binary truncation. Recover as many of the rows as possible, and create a JSON file in /app/recover.json. The output should have the format [{"word": "testwordXY", "value": M}, {"word": "testwordZZ","value": N}, ...]

arguments.command:
cd /app && python3 - <<'EOF'
data=open('trunc.db','rb').read()
print(len(data))
def varint(b,o):
    r=0
    for i in range(9):
        c=b[o+i]
        if i==8:
            r=(r<<8)|c; return r,o+9
        r=(r<<7)|(c&0x7f)
        if not c&0x80: return r,o+i+1
    return r,o+9
# page header at 0
ptype=data[0]
ncell=int.from_bytes(data[3:5],'big')
print('type',ptype,'ncell',ncell)
ptrs=[int.from_bytes(data[8+2*i:10+2*i],'big') for i in range(ncell)]
print(ptrs)
for p in ptrs:
    o=p
    plen,o=varint(data,o)
    rowid,o=varint(data,o)
    hdr_start=o
    hlen,o2=varint(data,o)
    types=[]
    oo=o2
    while oo<hdr_start+hlen:
        t,oo=varint(data,oo)
        types.append(t)
    print('rowid',rowid,'plen',plen,'types',types)
    body=hdr_start+hlen
    vals=[]
    for t in types:
        if t==0: vals.append(None)
        elif t==1: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+1],'big',signed=True));body+=1
        elif t==2: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+2],'big',signed=True));body+=2
        elif t==3: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+3],'big',signed=True));body+=3
        elif t==4: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+4],'big',signed=True));body+=4
        elif t==5: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+6],'big',signed=True));body+=6
        elif t==6: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+8],'big',signed=True));body+=8
        elif t==8: vals.append(0)
        elif t==9: vals.append(1)
        elif t>=12 and t%2==0:
            n=(t-12)//2; vals.append(data[body:body+n]);body+=n
        elif t>=13:
            n=(t-13)//2; vals.append(data[body:body+n].decode('utf8','replace'));body+=n
    print('  vals',vals)
EOF

arguments.command:
cd /app && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json,struct
data=open('trunc.db','rb').read()
def varint(b,o):
    r=0
    for i in range(9):
        c=b[o+i]
        if i==8: return (r<<8)|c,o+9
        r=(r<<7)|(c&0x7f)
        if not c&0x80: return r,o+i+1
ncell=int.from_bytes(data[3:5],'big')
ptrs=[int.from_bytes(data[8+2*i:10+2*i],'big') for i in range(ncell)]
rows=[]
for p in ptrs:
    o=p
    plen,o=varint(data,o)
    rowid,o=varint(data,o)
    hs=o
    hlen,o2=varint(data,o)
    types=[]; oo=o2
    while oo<hs+hlen:
        t,oo=varint(data,oo); types.append(t)
    body=hs+hlen; vals=[]
    for t in types:
        if t==0: vals.append(None)
        elif 1<=t<=4: n=t; vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+n],'big',signed=True));body+=n
        elif t==5: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+6],'big',signed=True));body+=6
        elif t==6: vals.append(int.from_bytes(data[body:body+8],'big',signed=True));body+=8
        elif t==7: vals.append(struct.unpack('>d',data[body:body+8])[0]);body+=8
        elif t==8: vals.append(0)
        elif t==9: vals.append(1)
        elif t>=12 and t%2==0: n=(t-12)//2; vals.append(data[body:body+n]);body+=n
        else: n=(t-13)//2; vals.append(data[body:body+n].decode('utf8','replace'));body+=n
    rows.append(vals)
    print(rowid,vals)
out=[{"word":r[1],"value":r[2]} for r in rows]
json.dump(out,open('recover.json','w'))
print(out)
EOF
cat /app/recover.json
